To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the primordial power and bispectrum can be modified in the presence of a turning trajectory and that the modifications are related to a non-trivial speed of sound.

the power spectrum of adiabatic perturbations in multi-field models can be significantly altered by turns in the trajectory of the inflatons, and that the speed of sound of the adiabatics can also be significantly altered in this way.
the power spectrum is modified by the presence of a bend in the inflaton trajectory, and the modification takes the form of damps superimposed oscillatory modes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the power spectrum of inflationary perturbations is a faithful messenger from the high energy regime of inflation.
the study of the interplay between the dynamics of the inflaton field(s) and the evolution of the curvature perturbation in multi-field inflation.
the question of how the physics of a heavy field affects the primordial power spectra in multi-field inflation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of turning trajectories in multi-field inflation generically leads to a modified speed of propagation of adiabatic modes, and hence to the possibility of observable imprints in both the power spectrum and non-Gaussianity.
, in multi-field inflation, turning is generically a feature of the inflaton trajectory which may lead to significant deviations from the canonical single-field predictions.
the presence of turns in the background inflaton trajectories may be a smoking gun for heavy physics in multi-field inflationary models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, even if the inflaton traverses a bend during inflation, the adiabat remains well-defined, but the effective theory of the adiabatics becomes more complicated.
the power spectrum in a general multi-field inflation model can be written as an integral over all the inflaton trajectories.
the power spectrum in multi-dimensional inflationary models may be affected by the presence of heavy modes even if the latter are far above the cutoff of our effective theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of multi-field inflation, it is not sufficient to only look for features in the primordial curvature perturbation.

the power spectrum of a multi-field inflation model is sensitive to the details of the background trajectory, and in particular to its turns, even if these occur on a time scale much shorter than that of inflation.
, in the context of inflationary models where the inflaton traverses a bend in field space, we can no longer assume that the adiabatics are the only degrees of freedom that matter.
